_comment: Tool directory entries. Editable by non-engineers. `universityProvided: true` marks tools provided/endorsed by U-M. Any tool with universityProvided:false MUST render the non-University warning wherever it appears. `approvalStatusNote` is intentionally soft-coded because university-approved status can change — keep it current. DRAFT placeholder content: confirm all details against current U-M/ITS guidance before relying on it.

tools.name: U-M GPT
tools.label: University-provided
tools.shortDescription: U-M's secure, general-purpose generative AI chat built on leading foundation models, with university data protections.
tools.dataSensitivityNote: Offers stronger data protections than public consumer chatbots. Confirm current data-handling guidance in ITS documentation before entering any sensitive, regulated, or confidential information.
strengths: Free for U-M staff and students
University data protections vs. public tools
General-purpose and easy to access with U-M credentials
limitations: Not a substitute for authoritative sources; can still hallucinate
Approved data-sensitivity level should be confirmed for regulated data
Not specialized for any single domain
tools.bestFor: Everyday drafting, summarizing, and general questions where no confidential data is involved.
tools.accessPath: Sign in with your U-M credentials at the U-M GPT service (see ITS AI services page for the current URL).

tools.name: U-M Maizey
tools.label: University-provided
tools.shortDescription: U-M's tool for building custom AI assistants grounded in your own documents and data sources (retrieval-augmented).
approvedFor: Answering questions over a defined set of your own documents
Building a project- or team-specific assistant
Summarizing and searching curated internal content
tools.dataSensitivityNote: Because Maizey can be pointed at your own data sources, be especially deliberate about what you upload. Confirm the data classification allowed for your project in current ITS guidance.
strengths: Grounds answers in your provided sources (reduces hallucination)
limitations: Quality depends on the quality/scope of the sources you provide
Setup effort to curate and maintain the knowledge base
tools.bestFor: Question-answering and summarization grounded in a specific, curated set of documents you control.
tools.accessPath: Access Maizey with your U-M credentials via the ITS AI services page; create a project and add your data sources.

tools.name: Gemini
tools.label: University-provided
tools.shortDescription: Google's generative AI, available to U-M under the Google Workspace agreement. Approval scope can change — confirm current status.
approvedFor: Drafting and summarizing within approved Google Workspace contexts
General assistance integrated with Google tools
tools.dataSensitivityNote: Availability and approved data classifications depend on the current U-M Google Workspace agreement. Do not assume a data level — confirm current approval status in the Tool Directory / ITS guidance before use.
strengths: Integrated with Google Workspace apps many staff already use
Covered under an existing university agreement
limitations: Approval scope and data-handling terms can change over time
Confirm current U-M approval status before relying on it
tools.bestFor: General drafting and assistance for staff already working inside Google Workspace, once current approval status is confirmed.
tools.accessPath: Available through U-M Google Workspace where enabled; confirm current access and approval status with ITS.
